newsitem.title: UK: Moderate UK minimum wage would limit damage - CBI.
newsitem.headline: Moderate UK minimum wage would limit damage - CBI.

text.p: British jobs would be lost if a minimum wage was introduced, but if it was set at a moderate level the damage would be minimised, the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) said on Monday.

"We disagree in principle, but the level of a minimum wage will become much more important than the principle," Andrew Buxton, chairman of the CBI's economic affairs committee, told reporters at the CBI annual conference.
"There is absolutely no doubt that at 4.26 stg, jobs will be lost. But at 3.50 stg, fewer jobs would go," he said.
The opposition Labour Party is committed to introducing a national minimum wage if it wins the general election. The Trades Union Congress has called for a minimum wage to be set at 4.26 stg.
Buxton said the CBI was also concerned about the future implications of the European Union's Social Chapter, which guarantees minimum working rights and from which Britain currently has an opt-out.
"At the moment, the Social Chapter does not bring in many problems. It's more what the future holds."

He said the system of majority voting on Social Chapter issues could herald extra rules and regulation for businesses in the future which would prove more costly. "Majority voting opens the door to quite a lot."
Speaking earlier on BBC radio, Labour Party finance spokesman Gordon Brown said a Labour government would sign up for the Social Chapter, but would veto attempts to extend majority voting.
